issues.description: Using Math.random() for ID generation is cryptographically insecure and may lead to collisions or predictable IDs that could be exploited to access other users' data
issues.suggestion: Use crypto.randomUUID() for secure, unpredictable unique identifiers: `function generateId(): string { return crypto.randomUUID(); }`

issues.description: Email regex is overly permissive and may accept invalid emails (e.g., multiple @ signs, missing TLD validation), potentially allowing malformed data into the system
issues.suggestion: Use a more robust email validation library or regex, or consider using a validation library like Zod: `z.string().email()`

issues.description: HTML entity encoding is incomplete and context-dependent; this approach may not prevent XSS in all contexts (e.g., inside script tags, event handlers, or URLs)
issues.suggestion: Use a well-tested sanitization library like DOMPurify for HTML contexts, or simply use textContent/innerText when inserting into DOM to avoid HTML parsing entirely

issues.description: Empty string validation using truthy check will fail for whitespace-only strings; should explicitly check for non-empty trimmed strings
issues.suggestion: Use explicit validation: `if (!input.email?.trim() || !input.name?.trim()) { throw new Error('Email and name are required'); }`

codeQuality.summary: Well-structured code with good security practices (parameterized queries, input validation, sanitization), but uses insecure Math.random() for ID generation which poses a medium security risk.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email validation is security-critical for preventing invalid data entry and potential injection attacks. The regex pattern needs thorough testing for edge cases (multiple @, missing domain, special characters, unicode, etc.)
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: describe('isValidEmail', () => { it('rejects email with multiple @ symbols', () => { expect(isValidEmail('user@@example.com')).toBe(false); }); it('rejects email without domain extension', () => { expect(isValidEmail('user@example')).toBe(false); }); it('accepts valid standard email', () => { expect(isValidEmail('user@example.com')).toBe(true); }); it('rejects email with spaces', () => { expect(isValidEmail('user @example.com')).toBe(false); }); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: XSS prevention is absolutely critical for security. This function must be thoroughly tested to ensure all dangerous characters are properly escaped and cannot be bypassed with encoding tricks or edge cases.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: describe('sanitizeInput', () => { it('escapes < and > to prevent tag injection', () => { expect(sanitizeInput('')).toBe('<script>alert(1)</script>'); }); it('escapes quotes to prevent attribute injection', () => { expect(sanitizeInput('"onclick="alert(1)"')).toBe('"onclick="alert(1)"'); }); it('handles combined injection attempts', () => { expect(sanitizeInput('')).toBe('<img src="x" onerror='alert(1)'>'); }); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: This is the main user creation flow handling data validation, sanitization, and persistence. Untested error paths (missing fields, invalid email) could allow corrupted data into the database or expose security vulnerabilities.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: describe('createUser', () => { it('throws error when email is missing', async () => { await expect(createUser({ email: '', name: 'John' })).rejects.toThrow('Email and name are required'); }); it('throws error when name is missing', async () => { await expect(createUser({ email: 'test@example.com', name: '' })).rejects.toThrow('Email and name are required'); }); it('throws error for invalid email format', async () => { await expect(createUser({ email: 'invalid-email', name: 'John' })).rejects.toThrow('Invalid email format'); }); it('creates user with sanitized name and lowercase email', async () => { const user = await createUser({ email: 'Test@Example.COM', name: '<script>Evil</script>' }); expect(user.email).toBe('test@example.com'); expect(user.name).toBe('<script>Evil</script>'); expect(user.id).toMatch(/^user_/); expect(user.createdAt).toBeInstanceOf(Date); }); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: ID generation uniqueness is important for data integrity. If IDs collide, it could cause data corruption or user record conflicts. The current implementation using Date.now() + Math.random() should be tested for format and potential collision scenarios.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: describe('generateId', () => { it('generates ID with user_ prefix', () => { const id = generateId(); expect(id).toMatch(/^user_\d+_[a-z0-9]{7}$/); }); it('generates unique IDs on consecutive calls', () => { const ids = new Set([generateId(), generateId(), generateId(), generateId(), generateId()]); expect(ids.size).toBe(5); }); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: Error-handling branches for missing/invalid input are critical to prevent bad data from entering the system. Each validation branch (missing email, missing name, invalid email format) needs explicit assertion.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: describe('createUser error branches', () => { it('validates missing email before checking format', async () => { await expect(createUser({ email: '', name: 'Test' })).rejects.toThrow('Email and name are required'); }); it('validates email format after presence check', async () => { await expect(createUser({ email: 'bad-email', name: 'Test' })).rejects.toThrow('Invalid email format'); }); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: XSS attackers use edge cases like null bytes, unicode lookalikes, nested encoding, and empty strings to bypass sanitization. These must be tested to ensure the function is robust.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: describe('sanitizeInput edge cases', () => { it('handles empty string', () => { expect(sanitizeInput('')).toBe(''); }); it('handles string with no special characters', () => { expect(sanitizeInput('Hello World')).toBe('Hello World'); }); it('handles multiple consecutive special chars', () => { expect(sanitizeInput('<<<>>>')).toBe('<<<>>>'); }); it('handles mixed quotes', () => { expect(sanitizeInput('"Hello\'s world"')).toBe('"Hello's world"'); }); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email validation regex can miss edge cases like leading/trailing dots, consecutive dots, or international characters. These edge cases could allow invalid emails through or reject valid ones.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: describe('isValidEmail edge cases', () => { it('rejects empty string', () => { expect(isValidEmail('')).toBe(false); }); it('rejects email with leading dot', () => { expect(isValidEmail('.user@example.com')).toBe(false); }); it('rejects email with trailing dot in domain', () => { expect(isValidEmail('user@example.com.')).toBe(false); }); it('rejects email with consecutive dots', () => { expect(isValidEmail('user..name@example.com')).toBe(false); }); });
